_about: Batch B2b (Engine core). Owner: the B2b writer. Terms for the engine core process, async scheduling, executors and workers. Reused, not redefined: engine-core (alias EngineCoreProc), busy-loop, batch-queue, output-placeholder, async-scheduling (t1), utility-call (b2a), executor, worker (core).

input-thread.short: A daemon thread in the engine core process. It receives requests on the ZMQ sockets, decodes them, builds the Request object and puts it into input_queue.

output-thread.short: A daemon thread in the engine core process. It takes EngineCoreOutputs from output_queue, encodes them with msgpack and sends them on a ZMQ PUSH socket to the front end.

max-concurrent-batches.short: The number of engine steps that can be in flight at the same time. It sets the size of the batch queue: pp_size + 1 with async scheduling and Model Runner V2, so 2 on one GPU.

uni-executor.short: The executor backend "uni" (UniProcExecutor). It makes the one worker as an object in the engine core process and calls its methods directly. By default, vLLM uses it only when TP = PP = DP = 1.

multiproc-executor.short: The executor backend "mp" (MultiprocExecutor). It starts one worker process per local rank and sends every call to all of them through one shared-memory message queue.

worker-proc.short: The wrapper that runs one worker in its own process (named VllmWorker-0, VllmWorker-1, ...). Its busy loop reads calls from the broadcast message queue and writes the results into its own reply queue.

collective-rpc.short: The executor method that runs one worker method (by name, or a pickled function) on every worker and collects the results. execute_model and sample_tokens use it too.

message-queue.short: vLLM's one-writer, many-reader queue in shared memory (a ring buffer of chunks). Large messages go over a ZMQ socket instead. The multiproc executor uses it to talk to its workers.

profile-run.short: A forward pass with dummy inputs of max_num_batched_tokens tokens at start-up. vLLM measures the peak memory of this pass to compute how much memory is left for the KV cache.
